security_audit.summary: Most shell backtick alerts are Markdown fence or inline-code false positives, and the visible project commands use fixed paths. The main confirmed issue is automatic access to a hidden home Claude-mem settings file. A semantic review also found unnecessary Write permission for a session orientation workflow.

remediation.suggestion: Do not read $HOME/.claude-mem/settings.json automatically. Ask for explicit consent or use a tool-provided status command that does not expose private configuration files.
Remove Write from allowed-tools unless this skill is changed to perform documented file modifications.
Replace cat, grep, and cut parsing with a safer structured read flow, or require user confirmation before running Bash commands.

content.user_title: Start Coding Sessions With Project Context
content.value_statement: Developers lose time reconstructing project status at session start. This skill checks repository state, task files, and guidance before proposing next work.
actual_capabilities: Checks Plans.md and session-log.md line counts and suggests cleanup when files grow large.
Detects Claude-mem harness mode when its settings file is present.
Runs git status and recent git log commands for repository context.
Reads Plans.md and AGENTS.md to identify active tasks and project constraints.
Produces a concise session report with priority tasks, cautions, and a next action.
limitations: Requires Plans.md and AGENTS.md for the most complete session report.
Uses Bash and local file reads, so it should run only in trusted workspaces.
Does not implement tasks or modify code by itself.
Claude-mem context appears only when Claude-mem is installed and configured.

use_cases.title: Resume a development session
use_cases.description: Review branch status, recent commits, open tasks, and project rules before continuing work.

use_cases.title: Prepare an AI coding assistant
use_cases.description: Load the relevant task list and repository guidance before asking the assistant to start work.

use_cases.title: Coordinate planned project work
use_cases.description: Find pending PM requests, work in progress, and assigned tasks from Plans.md.

prompt_templates.title: Start Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Start my coding session and show the current project status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user wants a simple orientation report.

prompt_templates.title: Check Before Choosing Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the repository status, task files, and project guidance before I choose a task.
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants context before selecting a work item.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend Priority Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Plans.md and AGENTS.md, then recommend the highest priority task to start now.
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants a task recommendation based on local planning files.

prompt_templates.title: Full Session Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize the session with git context, Claude-mem context if available, task priority, constraints, and one next action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user wants a complete startup brief before implementation.

output_examples.output: Session brief with the current branch, recent commits, priority tasks from Plans.md, key AGENTS.md cautions, and a suggested next action.

output_examples.input: What should I work on first?
output_examples.output: A ranked task recommendation that favors PM-requested work and continuing work in progress, with context from project guidance.
A concise status report covering repository state, task files, optional memory context, and cleanup suggestions for large files.

best_practices: Run it only inside trusted project workspaces because it reads local status files.
Keep Plans.md and AGENTS.md current so the session report is accurate.
Review the suggested next action before starting implementation work.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a task runner; it is for orientation and planning.
Do not run it in directories that contain unrelated private files.
Do not rely on it when project guidance files are missing or stale.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It checks Git status, recent commits, Plans.md, AGENTS.md, and optional Claude-mem context.

faq.question: Does it change project files?
faq.answer: The documented workflow is for inspection and reporting. It should not modify files during session startup.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it at the start of a coding session or when you need to choose the next task.

faq.question: Does it require Claude-mem?
faq.answer: No. Claude-mem context is optional and is skipped when the settings file is absent.

faq.question: Can it work without Plans.md?
faq.answer: It can still report repository status, but task recommendations are limited without Plans.md.

faq.question: Is it suitable for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: No. It uses Bash and local file reads, so it should be limited to trusted workspaces.
